text:
Maria Chen: eu-west-1 GPU pool is exhausted — tons of Pending pods from a research sweep, dashboards spiking. Anyone oncall? :boom:
AJ Park: seeing ~120 Pending, nodes at 100% GPU alloc. Autoscaler not creating new nodepool, it keeps queuing scale up then fails.
Neal Torres: logs show CA requests being rejected with ENI allocation error in the cloud provider: "AttachNetworkInterface: quota exceeded" — ENI pool in eu-west-1 low.
Jen SRE: autoscaler-bot is spamming events: 
autoscaler-bot: scale_up rejected (nodegroup=fallback-gpu): failed to create instance: ENI quota exhausted.
Leo Patel: hmm — research sweep launched 200 jobs with nodeSelector: gpu=true and tolerations that match only our legacy-gpu pool. That pool is on-demand and fully utilized.
Samir Gupta: can we patch the jobs to allow the newer gpu nodepool? They have toleration for taint "legacy-gpu=true:NoSchedule" which blocks scheduling elsewhere.
Maria Chen: anyone can run a quick patch to remove that toleration? We need pods running.
AJ Park: I can do a temporary rollout to change tolerations + add nodeAffinity to prefer legacy, not require. Doing a kubectl patch now.
AJ Park: patch applied to jobset/rl-sweep-2026: removed strict toleration and added preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity.
Neal Torres: good — a bunch of pods moved but cluster still slow because CA keeps failing due to ENI. We should open a short-term mitigation: create a small on-demand fallback nodepool in a different subnet with spare ENI quota.
Jen SRE: I started creating a small fallback-gpu-on-demand (3 nodes) in eu-west-1b in a subnet with free ENI. Cloud console shows creation in progress.
autoscaler-bot: new nodegroup fallback-gpu-on-demand created, applying labels.
Leo Patel: once nodes register, we should taint them + add a temporary nodeSelector to the most urgent jobs, then remove taint later. That reduces noisy-scheduling on legacy pool.
Samir Gupta: starting an emergency admission patch: update PodTemplate for high-priority jobs (priorityClass=critical-infra) to include nodeSelector: fallback-nodepool=true.
AJ Park: applied. 27 pods bound to new nodes now. CPU/GPU pressure eased.
Maria Chen: queue drained from 120 Pending -> 14 Pending in ~6mins. Thanks team. :relieved:
Neal Torres: root cause summary: research sweep had a broken job template that required legacy-gpu toleration (mutating webhook updated jobs incorrectly during the sweep deploy). Autoscaler couldn't scale the only compatible pool because ENI quota prevented new instances.
Jen SRE: immediate mitigations we did:
- patched jobs to relax tolerations
- created small fallback nodepool in different subnet
- used nodeSelector to move critical pods
- applied temporary priorityClass to preempt low-priority batch pods
- alerted cloud quota team for ENI uplift

AJ Park: follow-ups for next hour: set quota alert for ENI at 60% used in eu-west-1, add a preflight check in the research job submit flow to validate tolerations/nodeSelectors, and add a safety limiter that caps concurrent job launches per team.
Samir Gupta: also adding a CI check to the mutating webhook to prevent it from overwriting tolerations for jobs labeled "sweep".
Leo Patel: cost note: fallback on-demand nodes will bump this run's bill by ~+$3k/hr if we keep them. Let's drain and deprovision as soon as safe.
Maria Chen: agreed — Jen, can you coordinate deprovision once backlog <5 and steady for 10m?
Jen SRE: yes. I'll monitor and deprovision fallback nodes when stable.
autoscaler-bot: scale activity: new nodes added=3, nodes removed=0, pending requests=0.
AJ Park: postmortem items I've captured:
- fix mutating webhook test coverage (Samir)
- ENI quota alert and runbook update (Neal)
- research job submitter preflight + throttling (Leo)
- add CA fallback policy to attempt cross-subnet launches when ENI errors occur (Maria)

Maria Chen: thanks all — great triage. Filing an incident ticket with the above actions and tagging the research team for follow-up. We'll schedule a retro with cost impact. :note:
Neal Torres: marking this as mitigated. Last pending dropped at 2471123508.
Jen SRE: deprovision scheduled at 2471123600 unless we get new spikes.
Maria Chen: closing thread here, open follow-ups in #incidents-postmortems.
